# What's tested

<!-- Generated by scripts/test_map.py from the test files themselves; do not edit by hand.
     CI fails when this page is out of date: run `python3 scripts/test_map.py` and commit it. -->

PsyNeuView's automated tests, feature by feature: what each area's tests check, at which layer, whether CI runs them on every pull request, and the issue each one guards. Below that are the coverage numbers, how well the canvas agrees with PsyNeuLink's own `show_graph`, the browser tests CI doesn't run and why, and the known gaps. For how the suites and CI fit together, see [Testing & CI](testing.md).

## At a glance

| Layer | Files | Tests | Run by CI on every pull request |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser (Playwright) | 160 | 433 | 421 tests in 154 files |
| Tutorial walkthrough | 35 | 80 | 80 tests in 35 files |
| Frontend unit (vitest) | 134 | 1204 | 1204 tests in 134 files |
| Backend (pytest) | 188 | 1749 | 1749 tests in 188 files |

A browser test runs in CI when its file is listed in `frontend/e2e/ci-specs.txt` and the test (or the `describe` around it) is tagged `@ci`; every tutorial walkthrough runs in the tutorials job; every unit and backend test runs, bar those marked skip or expected-to-fail.

## Agreement with show_graph

`e2e/show-graph-agreement.spec.ts` opens every bundled model in every view, lays it out Like show_graph, and scores the canvas against show_graph's own picture. Full batch measured 2026-11-23 at commit `44ce5d77d4`: **174 of 175** views agree fully on nodes, rows and order.

**What CI holds it to.** The `@ci` test opens four representative models: the basic Stroop reference, EGO in each of its views (nested, flattened, PyTorch), folded in each, and with CIMs shown, MontagueDayanSejnowski96 (learning), and `demos/nested_compositions.py` (a composition open inside another). In every view it requires all of show_graph's nodes on the canvas, rows and order at 100%, no overlapping boxes, nothing cut off after Fit, no frame button covered, and every edge show_graph draws between two canvas nodes drawn along its course (no exceptions are listed). Measured with the full batch: all of those pass at 100%. The full batch below has no thresholds; it is run before a release and its review sheets looked at.

Nodes: show_graph's nodes the canvas draws. Rows: pairs of nodes whose above, level or below relation agrees. Order: pairs on one show_graph row whose left-to-right order agrees. Courses: edges drawn along show_graph's own course.

**Below 100%**, and why:

| Model | View | Nodes | Rows | Order | Courses | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stroop_with_control | the model · Controller hidden | 9/9 | 81% | 100% | 8/9 | Probably a measurement taken too early: the review sheet shows the canvas still busy (its spinner at 8 s) with the controller already hidden, while the show_graph picture the batch compared it with still draws CONTROL. With the controller shown, the same model agrees 100%. Not yet confirmed. |

## Browser tests CI doesn't run

6 browser spec files aren't in CI at all. Each says why in a `Not in CI:` line in its header; this table is read from those lines. (Every tutorial runs, in the tutorials job.)

| Spec | Why | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `_measure-load-latency.spec.ts` | measurement | it only logs load timings, with no assertions; run it with PERF_MEASURE=1 when measuring |
| `_measure-undo-memory.spec.ts` | measurement | it only logs heap use, with no assertions; run it with PERF_MEASURE=1 when measuring |
| `docs-shots-saving.spec.ts` | pictures only | it retakes the docs' pictures; the behaviour is tested by saves-in-history and changes-since-save |
| `editor-drag-select.spec.ts` | broken | on the Linux runners the forwards-and-backwards test finds |
| `pycharm-live.local.spec.ts` | local only | it drives a real PyCharm on macOS, which the runners don't have; external-edit-sync.spec.ts is the CI version |
| `style-conventions.spec.ts` | broken | two tests fail on devel, expecting 13px buttons that the default Text size (1.1, since #111) draws at 14.3px; tracked in #322. Fix, then add |

Spec files in CI that hold tests CI skips (untagged, or a measurement run only on request):

- `fit-frames-edges.spec.ts`: every reference model: after Fit nothing is cut off and no course has a spike, in ${size.name}
- `show-graph-agreement.spec.ts`: every bundled model, every view: agreement with show_graph

## Running each layer locally

```bash
# Backend (from backend/, with its .venv)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -n auto
# ... with coverage, then fold in what the model-runner processes wrote as they
# exited (after pytest-cov's own report), and write backend/coverage.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -n auto --cov --cov-report=
.venv/bin/python -m coverage combine --append && .venv/bin/python -m coverage json

# Frontend unit tests (from frontend/)
npm test
npm run test:coverage        # writes frontend/coverage/coverage-summary.json

# Browser tests (from frontend/; builds, then starts its own backend on a free port)
npm run test:e2e:ci          # what the e2e check runs on a pull request
npx playwright test e2e/drag-to-connect.spec.ts   # one spec
npx playwright test e2e/tutorials                 # the tutorials job
npx playwright test e2e/show-graph-agreement.spec.ts -g 'every bundled'  # the full agreement batch

# This page (from the repo root)
python3 scripts/test_map.py
python3 scripts/test_map.py --coverage backend/coverage.json frontend/coverage/coverage-summary.json
python3 scripts/test_map.py --agreement frontend/test-results/show-graph-agreement/agreement.json
```

## Known gaps

Found while building this page (#319). Each is a gap in what the tests check, not a known bug in the app, except where it says so.

- **A model built in the UI against the same model typed as code: now covered** for Mapping, Control, Gating and Learning projections and one into a nested composition (`ui-text-equivalence.spec.ts`, with `backend/tests/model_equivalence.py`). Not yet covered: projections between nested compositions, control of a nested node's parameter, and models whose nodes the UI builds with non-default parameters.
- **Round trips: now covered** for adding, deleting, renaming and connecting nodes and changing a parameter (`round-trips.spec.ts`); shaping an arrow was already covered by `edge-curve-handles.spec.ts`. Renaming or deleting an arrow is covered one way only (`graph-arrow-menus.spec.ts`).
- **`style-conventions.spec.ts` is broken on devel** (#322). Its two tests expect 13px buttons; the default Text size (1.1, since #111) draws them at 14.3px. It isn't in CI, so nothing failed. Fifteen other specs CI used to skip now run in it; `editor-drag-select.spec.ts` stays out until its selection check works on the Linux runners.
- **The React components have no unit tests.** Frontend line coverage is about a quarter, because `components/` is tested only in the browser, which coverage can't see. The feature map is the measure for those.
- **Frontend logic modules with little unit coverage:** `utils/labels.ts`, `utils/nodeActions.ts`, `hooks/useFileWatcher.ts` and `stores/edgeAttachStore.ts` are each a quarter covered or less, and `stores/modelStore.ts`, the biggest store, about half.
- **The AI assistant's tests are not on devel.** Its runner-guard and OS-sandbox suites live on the assistant branch, so this page shows that area empty.
- **The Mac app's side of its bridges.** The browser tests stand in for the Mac app by answering its messages; the native side is tested in the Mac app's own repository, not here.
- **Test counts are test functions.** A parametrized backend test, or a browser test written in a loop, counts once here; pytest itself reports about 2,100 backend tests.
- **Do the tests check what they claim?** In a sample of five deliberate breakages (#319: the drag-to-connect type rule, the role colours, writing a projection, show_graph's left-to-right order, the click-never-connects threshold), each was caught by at least one CI test.
- **show_graph agreement, outside the representative models.** The full batch (above) finds EGO's flattened and PyTorch views falling back from Like show_graph after their compositions are folded, and 28 views with something cut off after Fit; the `@ci` test covers neither. It also scores the canvas against a picture laid out by the same `placementFromGraphviz` the canvas uses, so a mistake in that function would move both sides and go unseen; `showGraphLayout.test.ts` is what guards it.

Areas with no tests on this branch: AI assistant.
